title: WOULD THE LORD HAVE BEEN PLEASED?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Aaron replied to Moses, 'Today they sacrificed their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, but such things as this have happened to me. Would the LORD have been pleased if I had eaten the sin offering today?'" - Lev 10:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron finally speaks. His first recorded words since his sons died.

Such things as this have happened to me. He does not say more than that. He does not name them or describe what he saw. The grief is contained in a phrase.

And then his question, which is really an appeal: would God truly have wanted me to sit down and eat a fellowship meal today, of all days?

Aaron is not defying the law. He is asking whether its purpose was being served. The sin offering was to be eaten as part of the priest's ministry on behalf of the people. Could a man in his condition, that day, have done that meaningfully?

It is a careful, humble, honest question — and Scripture records it without a word of rebuke.

God is not offended by our honest questions. The Psalms are full of them. How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? (Ps 13:1). Jesus Himself cried out, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? (Mtt 27:46).

There is a difference between defying God and bringing Him your honest bewilderment. He has never minded the second.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I feel free to bring God my honest questions, or do I think He requires only agreement?
2. What have I been carrying that I have never actually said to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You receive honest questions. Here is what I do not understand — I bring it to You rather than hiding it. Amen.
